record.paper_title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
record.original_question: Given a countably infinite homogeneous structure K, determine the full hierarchy of its big Ramsey theory: first, whether K has finite big Ramsey degrees for every finite substructure; second, if finite degrees exist, whether the exact degrees can be characterized by canonical partitions and then calculated or algorithmically computed; and third, whether K carries a big Ramsey structure, meaning an optimal finite expansion whose finite substructures have big Ramsey degree one with coherent unavoidable colorings.

evidence.quote: A structure K is homogeneous if each isomorphism between finite substructures of K extends to an automorphism of K.

Question 2.3. Given a homogeneous structure K, (1) Does K have finite big Ramsey degrees? That is, can one find upper bounds ensuring that big Ramsey degrees exist? (2) If K has finite big Ramsey degrees, is there a characterization of the exact big Ramsey degrees via canonical partitions? If yes, calculate or find an algorithm to calculate them. (3) Does K carry a big Ramsey structure?
A big Ramsey structure is essentially a finite expansion K∗ of K so that each finite substructure of K∗ has big Ramsey degree one

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A relational structure K on a countably infinite domain is called homogeneous if every isomorphism between two finite substructures of K extends to an automorphism of K. For a finite substructure A of K, the big Ramsey degree of A in K is the least integer T (if it exists) such that for every finite coloring of the copies of A in K, there is an isomorphic copy K' of K inside K in which the copies of A take at most T colors; if no such integer exists, the big Ramsey degree is infinite. A big Ramsey structure for K is a finite-language expansion K* of K such that every finite substructure of K* has big Ramsey degree equal to one in K*, together with coherent unavoidable colorings of the copies of each finite substructure of K that witness the big Ramsey degrees in K.

For a given countably infinite homogeneous structure K, resolve the following three-level hierarchy:

(1) Does every finite substructure of K have finite big Ramsey degree in K (and provide upper bounds witnessing this)?

(2) Assuming finite big Ramsey degrees exist, characterize the exact big Ramsey degrees via canonical partitions of the copies of each finite substructure, and give an explicit formula or an algorithm to compute them.

(3) Does K carry a big Ramsey structure in the sense above?

artifact.status_search_result: The three-part program (finiteness of big Ramsey degrees, exact characterization via canonical partitions, and existence of big Ramsey structures) for arbitrary countably infinite homogeneous structures remains open as a general meta-question. Specific instances have been resolved (e.g., the generic partial order, the homogeneous K_4-free graph, ordered n-partite graphs and the SDAP+ class), but no general answer covering all homogeneous structures is known.

status_evidence.snippet: Presents current trends and open problems on big Ramsey degrees, including finiteness, exact computation, and big Ramsey structures.
status_evidence.claim: The three-tier question is posed as an open research program for homogeneous structures.

status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of big Ramsey degrees for the generic partial order.
status_evidence.claim: Specific cases are solved, indicating the general program is still being chipped away at.

status_evidence.title: Counting big Ramsey degrees of the homogeneous and universal K_4-free graph
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work computing big Ramsey degrees for the universal K_4-free graph.
status_evidence.claim: Continuing progress on specific homogeneous structures shows the general hierarchy remains an active open program.
